report:
### Conclusion
**The claim is unfounded.** There is no scientific evidence that taking ibuprofen or other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) worsens COVID-19 outcomes or exacerbates the infection.

### Evidence & Analysis
Early in the COVID-19 pandemic (March 2020), concern spread after anecdotal reports and a French government warning suggested that anti-inflammatory drugs like ibuprofen might worsen viral infections. 

However, subsequent clinical studies, large cohort evaluations, and systematic meta-analyses examined patient data and found no association between ibuprofen use and increased risk of hospitalization, disease severity, or mortality in COVID-19 patients. 

Major international public health organizations and regulatory bodies—including the World Health Organization (WHO), the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), and European medicines regulators—reviewed the evidence and confirmed that ibuprofen is safe for treating pain and fever caused by COVID-19 when used as directed.

### Sources
* World Health Organization: https://www.who.int/news-room/commentaries/detail/the-use-of-non-steroidal-anti-inflammatory-drugs-(nsaids)-in-patients-with-covid-19
* U.S. Food and Drug Administration: https://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-alerts-and-statements/fda-advises-patients-use-non-steroidal-anti-inflammatory-drugs-nsaids-covid-19
* Systematic Review & Meta-Analysis: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8327046/
* The BMJ Report: https://www.bmj.com/content/369/bmj.m1555
